instruction: Create a file 'bert_title.txt' on the Desktop containing the complete title of the BERT paper from the opened references document.

rules.expected: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

metadata.explanation: The BERT paper title is 'BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding'. Task requires finding and extracting this complete title. Verified by reading references.docx. Using fuzzy_match to ensure the complete title is present with high similarity.

llm_judge_reasons: CRITICAL: Type mismatch - fuzzy_match receives file path string, not file contents. The getter vm_file (file.py:74-143) returns the cached file path (e.g., '/tmp/cache/bert_title.txt'), but fuzzy_match (general.py:95-98) directly compares this path string to the expected title string without reading the file

Logic failure: fuzzy_match will compare '/tmp/cache/bert_title.txt' against 'BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding', which will always produce very low similarity scores and fail verification
No file content extraction: The evaluator never reads the file contents at all. The metric performs string comparison on the file path itself, not the text inside the file

Static warning confirmed: The warning 'metric fuzzy_match may not read vm_file result (no file/path usage detected)' correctly identifies that fuzzy_match doesn't open/read files - it just compares raw string values
Cannot verify instruction: The evaluator is fundamentally unable to verify whether the correct title was written to the file, as it never examines the file contents
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: CRITICAL FIX REQUIRED: Create a new metric that reads the file contents and then performs fuzzy matching. Example: 'def fuzzy_match_file_contents(file_path, rules): with open(file_path, 'r') as f: content = f.read().strip(); return fuzz.ratio(content, rules["expected"]) / 100.'

Alternative: Use file_contains metric with the complete title as expected value, though this only checks substring presence: {"func": "file_contains", "expected": {"type": "rule", "rules": {"expected": ["BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding"]}}}
Better alternative: Create a custom metric 'check_file_exact_match' that reads file and checks if stripped content exactly matches expected title, allowing minor whitespace variations

Best solution: Implement 'fuzzy_match_file_with_threshold' that reads file content, strips whitespace, and verifies fuzzy match score >= 0.9 against expected title to handle minor formatting differences while ensuring completeness
